## Services

- [Tax Planning & Optimisation](https://www.navigatewealth.co/tax-planning): Expert tax planning for individuals and businesses in South Africa — tax-efficient structures, estate duty, capital gains and corporate tax strategies.
- [Estate Planning](https://www.navigatewealth.co/estate-planning): Estate planning in South Africa — wills, trusts, succession planning, estate duty and business continuity, through our estate planning partners.
- [Financial Planning](https://www.navigatewealth.co/financial-planning): Independent financial planning in South Africa. Strategies covering investments, retirement, tax, estate planning & debt management.

- [Employee Benefits](https://www.navigatewealth.co/employee-benefits): Tailored employee benefits for businesses in South Africa. Group risk cover, retirement funds, medical aid & wellness programmes.

## Optional

- [Extortion on a building site is a cover question before it is a policing one](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/extortion-on-a-building-site-is-a-cover-question-first): Published 2026-11-18. Government reports more than 180 projects worth about R63 billion disrupted by construction extortion. For business owners the harder question is which policy, if any, responds when it happens.
- [A discretionary bonus is not yours until it is paid](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/a-discretionary-bonus-is-not-yours-until-it-is-paid): Published 2026-11-16. Many South Africans plan December around a bonus they have no legal right to receive. The difference between a guaranteed and a discretionary bonus decides what you can safely commit in advance.
- [Your offshore allowances reset on 1 January, and this year's are larger](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/your-offshore-allowances-reset-on-1-january): Published 2026-11-14. The single discretionary allowance doubled to R2 million this year. Both annual offshore allowances are measured by calendar year and reset on 1 January, with nothing carried forward, which leaves under two months of 2026 capacity.
- [When electricity injures, the supplier must disprove its own negligence](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/when-electricity-injures-the-supplier-must-disprove-negligence): Published 2026-11-14. A High Court judgment has held the national supplier fully liable for the electrocution of three children. The reason matters more than the facts: the law presumes the licensee was negligent until it proves otherwise.
- [Your insurer wants more data about you. POPIA sets the limits](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/your-insurer-wants-more-data-popia-decides-how-much): Published 2026-11-14. Telematics, wearables and longer application forms are making insurance pricing more individual. POPIA does not prevent that, but its conditions give a policyholder more leverage than most realise.
- [The university bill that arrives before the first lecture](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-university-bill-that-arrives-before-the-first-lecture): Published 2026-11-14. Registration and residence payments fall due in January, long before the year is paid for. We set out what the universities themselves now require up front, and how to plan for a cash demand of this size.
- [NHI is paused. Your medical scheme decisions are not](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/nhi-is-paused-your-medical-scheme-decisions-are-not): Published 2026-11-14. The Health Department has told Parliament not to expect National Health Insurance progress while the Constitutional Court judgment is outstanding. For households paying a medical scheme, that is not a reason to wait.
- [Your retirement pot is still locked. What Treasury has actually said](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/your-retirement-pot-is-still-locked-what-treasury-has-said): Published 2026-11-14. Talk of opening the preserved two-thirds of your retirement savings has resurfaced. We traced it to its source: a single passage in a Budget Review, no consultation paper, no draft clause and no law.
- [A defective will can sometimes be rescued. The rescue is a court application](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/a-defective-will-can-sometimes-be-rescued-by-a-court): Published 2026-11-14. A document that misses the signing formalities is not automatically worthless. It can be saved by a High Court order, but the cost, the delay and the burden of proof fall on the family left behind.
- [New councils must hold their first sitting within 14 days. Your municipal account is the reason to watch](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/new-councils-must-sit-within-14-days-your-municipal-account): Published 2026-11-14. The Electoral Commission declared the local government results on 8 November. In most councils no single party holds a majority, and the law gives them until roughly 22 November to elect mayors and speakers.
- [The largest crypto theft on record, and the question it puts to your own holdings](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/largest-crypto-theft-on-record-and-your-own-holdings): Published 2026-11-14. Roughly 6.4 billion dollars left a major exchange's wallets in a single afternoon in late October. The blockchain was not broken. The lesson for South African investors is about custody, not technology.
- [When one member's treatment costs millions, who pays for it?](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/when-one-members-treatment-costs-millions-who-pays-for-it): Published 2026-11-14. A scheme has been ordered to fund a rare-disease treatment in full, and the industry is now debating who should carry such costs. What the ruling means for your own cover and option choice.
- [Your savings pot allows one withdrawal a tax year. December is when that matters](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/your-savings-pot-allows-one-withdrawal-a-tax-year-december-is-when-that-matters): Published 2026-11-14. More than half of members who have drawn on their savings component have done so more than once. Before December, the tax, the timing rule and the order of decisions all deserve checking.
- [Your child can inherit at any age. Controlling the money is the harder part](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/your-child-can-inherit-at-any-age-controlling-the-money-is-the-harder-part): Published 2026-11-14. A valid bequest to a minor does not settle who holds the money, how it may be spent or when the child receives it. Where the will is silent, the Guardian's Fund or a fund's trustees decide.
- [A deregistration notice for a company that filed on time](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/a-deregistration-notice-for-a-company-that-filed-on-time): Published 2026-11-14. Companies that filed their annual returns, and companies too new to have defaulted, have received formal deregistration demands. Why the error still has to be answered, and what it threatens.
- [Offshore assets, two sets of death taxes, and one will that may not reach them](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/offshore-assets-two-sets-of-death-taxes-and-one-will): Published 2026-11-14. Offshore investing has become ordinary. The estate planning around it has not kept up. South African estate duty still applies to worldwide assets, and a second country may tax the same holding.
- [The SARS Commissioner does not phone you about a tax debt](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-sars-commissioner-does-not-phone-you-about-a-tax-debt): Published 2026-11-14. SARS has warned of a WhatsApp profile impersonating its Commissioner and phoning taxpayers about debt. A genuine tax debt follows a documented process you can verify yourself, without speaking to anyone.
- [Why your global index fund does not match the index](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/why-your-global-index-fund-does-not-match-the-index): Published 2026-11-14. Clients regularly ask why their offshore index fund has lagged the headline index. The usual answer is not the fund or its manager. It is the rand, and the effect is larger than most investors expect.
- [Fewer than one in four advice practices have started preparing for COFI](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/fewer-than-one-in-four-advice-practices-have-started-preparing-for-cofi): Published 2026-11-14. Six in ten advice professionals say they feel prepared for the coming conduct framework, but fewer than one in four have started formal preparation. We look at the gap and what closes it.
- [Unemployment at 33.7%, and the households that absorb it](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/unemployment-at-33-7-percent-and-the-households-that-absorb-it): Published 2026-11-14. Unemployment reached 33.7% in the third quarter even as the economy added 101 000 jobs. The planning consequence is not about markets; it is about who your household may end up supporting.
- [SARS has set out when it will fix an error without a formal dispute](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/sars-has-set-out-when-it-will-fix-an-error-without-a-formal-dispute): Published 2026-11-14. SARS has published guidance on when it will correct a mistake in an assessment without a formal objection. The route is narrow, the deadlines are unforgiving, and most taxpayers do not know it exists.
- [A divorce order can outrank the beneficiary form your insurer holds](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/a-divorce-order-can-outrank-the-beneficiary-form-your-insurer-holds): Published 2026-11-14. The Western Cape High Court has ordered a living annuity paid to a first wife rather than the nominated second wife, because a divorce settlement had already secured her right. We explain what that means for your own nominations.
- [The border declaration that is free, and the people charging for it](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-border-declaration-that-is-free-and-the-people-charging-for-it): Published 2026-11-14. SARS has reminded travellers that its online Traveller Declaration costs nothing, and that operators charging to complete it are not connected to SARS. What the declaration requires, and where it touches your offshore allowances.
- [What a retirement village's tax status says about how it is run](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/what-a-retirement-villages-tax-status-says-about-how-it-is-run): Published 2026-11-14. SARS has reissued its guidance on what a retirement village must do to qualify as a public benefit organisation. The requirements say a great deal about how these schemes are structured and funded.
- [Your adviser changes firms. What that means for you](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/your-adviser-changes-firms-what-that-means-for-you): Published 2026-11-14. A High Court ruling has confirmed that clients moving with a departing financial adviser is not, on its own, proof of solicitation. What the judgment decided, and what clients should check when their adviser moves.
- [Twelve funds is not a diversified portfolio](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/twelve-funds-is-not-a-diversified-portfolio): Published 2026-11-14. South Africans can choose from nearly two thousand local unit trust portfolios, and many investors end up holding several that do the same job. Why the number of funds says very little about diversification.
- [R50.4 trillion of missing cover, and the share of it that is yours](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/r50-4-trillion-of-missing-cover-and-the-share-of-it-that-is-yours): Published 2026-11-14. South Africa's life and disability insurance shortfall is measured at R50.4 trillion. The per-household version of that number is more useful: roughly R1.3 million of missing life cover and R1.8 million of missing disability cover.
- [A usufruct does not remove the asset from your estate](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/a-usufruct-does-not-remove-the-asset-from-your-estate): Published 2026-11-14. Usufructs, habitatios and fideicommissa appear in many South African wills. They split an asset rather than remove it, and the valuation rules can place most of its value exactly where you did not intend.
- [Tell your insurer when you first hear of it, not when the claim arrives](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/tell-your-insurer-when-you-first-hear-of-it): Published 2026-11-09. A notification clause can be a condition precedent to cover even when the policy never uses those words. The duty is triggered by what the insured knows, not by a formal demand, and the protections that follow a rejection cannot rescue a late notice.
- [There is no blacklist. There is a record, and most of it expires](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/there-is-no-blacklist-only-a-record-with-an-expiry-date): Published 2026-11-09. South African credit law has no list of banned borrowers. It has a credit record with legislated retention periods, and knowing which part lasts one year and which lasts five changes how you time a loan application.
- [Gap cover is paying out more than ever. Actuaries say that is part of the problem](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/gap-cover-paying-more-claims-and-the-shortfall-cycle): Published 2026-11-03. Seven in ten hospital events now produce a shortfall, and large gap cover claims are growing by double digits a year. Actuaries argue the two trends feed each other. We look at what that means for your cover.
- [South Africa scores 37 out of 100 on retirement adequacy](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/south-africa-scores-37-out-of-100-on-retirement-adequacy): Published 2026-10-28. The 2026 global pension index places South Africa 51st of 55 systems. The shape of the score matters more than the rank: strong governance, very weak adequacy, and most of the remedy sits with households.
- [The add-ons on your group cover are not the cover](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-add-ons-on-your-group-cover-are-not-the-cover): Published 2026-10-21. Group life and disability cover now arrives bundled with grocery benefits, virtual doctor consultations and legal advice lines. They are useful, and they are not what should decide the choice.
- [Compulsory or discretionary: the label on your money decides what you can do with it](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/compulsory-or-discretionary-money-what-each-one-allows): Published 2026-10-21. Two investments can hold identical assets and behave completely differently, because what governs them is the wrapper rather than the contents. Here are the rules, the 2026/27 limits and why the distinction matters.
- [The small policies that cost more than they ever pay out](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-small-policies-that-cost-more-than-they-ever-pay-out): Published 2026-10-21. Insurance earns its keep against losses you could not absorb. Where the payout is capped low, the excess is high and wear is excluded, the premium often buys less protection than it appears to.
- [When a property becomes hard to insure, the financial plan has to carry the gap](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/when-a-property-becomes-hard-to-insure): Published 2026-10-20. Insurers are repricing weather risk street by street rather than suburb by suburb. For homeowners the question is shifting from what cover costs to whether a particular risk will be accepted at all.
- [Two notches below investment grade, and the first positive outlook since 2007](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/two-notches-below-investment-grade-first-positive-outlook-since-2007): Published 2026-10-15. South Africa's sovereign credit rating has carried a positive outlook since May, its first in nearly two decades. We look at what an upgrade would and would not change in a client portfolio.
- [R1.5 trillion wagered, and the hole it leaves in a household plan](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/r1-5-trillion-wagered-and-the-hole-it-leaves-in-a-household-plan): Published 2026-10-15. South Africans wagered R1.5 trillion in a single financial year and lost R74.5 billion of it. We look at what that does to a household budget, and how it shows up in a financial plan.
- [Your income protection is a thirty-year promise. This is how the backing is measured](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/income-protection-is-a-long-promise-how-the-backing-is-measured): Published 2026-10-15. An industry survey reports that South African life insurers hold capital well above the regulatory minimum. We explain what that measure is, what it covers, and the things it tells you nothing about.
- [Who gets to vote when a company is in business rescue](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/who-gets-to-vote-when-a-company-is-in-business-rescue): Published 2026-10-13. The Constitutional Court has ruled that only creditors whose claims existed when business rescue began may vote on the rescue plan. For suppliers who keep trading, exposure grows while influence does not.
- [Pension savings are now reachable in more divorce claims](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/pension-savings-now-reachable-in-more-divorce-claims): Published 2026-10-13. The Constitutional Court has struck down the rule that kept retirement savings out of reach in divorce redistribution claims for marriages concluded after 1 November 1984 without accrual. We explain who is affected and what to review.
- [The will you signed may not be valid](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-will-you-signed-may-not-be-valid): Published 2026-10-12. An incorrectly signed will is one of the few planning failures that cannot be corrected afterwards, because the person who had to sign it is no longer there. The errors are small and common.
- [A proposal to pay medical negligence awards over time, not all at once](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/paying-medical-negligence-awards-over-time-not-all-at-once): Published 2026-10-12. The Law Reform Commission has proposed replacing once-off lump sums for medical negligence against the state with structured settlements paid over time. Two draft bills accompany the report, and none of it is law yet.
- [The Road Accident Fund owes R439 billion it does not have](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/raf-unfunded-liability-and-what-it-means-for-your-own-cover): Published 2026-10-10. Parliament was briefed this week on the Road Accident Fund's audited results. For families, the question is not governance but cash flow: who pays the bills while a claim waits five years or longer.
- [What a medical scheme's solvency ratio tells you](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/what-a-medical-schemes-solvency-ratio-tells-you): Published 2026-10-09. Most people choose a medical scheme on contribution and benefits. The solvency ratio is published every year, is rarely read, and is the clearest indication of whether a scheme can absorb a bad year.
- [The order you draw retirement income changes the tax you pay](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-order-you-draw-retirement-income-changes-the-tax-you-pay): Published 2026-10-09. Two retirees with identical assets and identical spending can pay very different amounts of tax. The difference is not the amount they draw, but which account they draw it from.
- [When the person taking your money was never licensed](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/when-the-person-taking-your-money-was-never-licensed): Published 2026-10-08. The Supreme Court of Appeal has confirmed that the business rescue moratorium does not cover assets a company neither owns nor lawfully holds. What that means for business owners and their personal exposure.

A South African bank has secured approval to hold digital assets for institutional clients. It is a real step in market structure, and it changes nothing about how crypto fits into a personal plan.
- [If SARS merged your tax profiles wrongly, you can now undo it yourself](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/unmerging-sars-efiling-profiles-what-to-check-after): Published 2026-10-05. SARS has made it possible to reverse an incorrectly merged eFiling profile without phoning the call centre. The function is genuinely useful, and it quietly resets details that matter during filing season, banking information among them.

Parliament has paused the Bill that lets the Reserve Bank move legacy contracts off JIBAR, three months before the benchmark is withdrawn. The same Bill opens the door to retiring the prime rate.
- [Most parents are planning for school fees. Fewer than half have a plan that holds](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/most-parents-planning-for-school-fees-fewer-have-a-plan): Published 2026-10-01. New research finds 86% of South African parents are thinking about education costs but only 49% have a structured plan, and six in ten pay fees from monthly salary. That is a funding method, not a plan.
- [The first 2027 medical scheme increases are in, at roughly double the benchmark](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/first-2027-medical-scheme-increases-double-the-benchmark): Published 2026-10-01. Momentum Medical Scheme has announced 7.9% for 2027 and Bestmed 7.35%, against a regulator benchmark of 3.8%. The gap is explainable, and the decisions it creates are yours to make before January.
- [Switching to vaping does not make you a non-smoker on your policy](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/switching-to-vaping-does-not-make-you-a-non-smoker): Published 2026-09-30. South African insurers generally rate any nicotine user as a smoker, vapers included. If your habit changed after your policy was underwritten, the disclosure question is one worth settling now rather than at claim stage.
- [The 30% wrapper: when an endowment earns its place, and when it does not](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/when-an-endowment-earns-its-place): Published 2026-09-30. An endowment taxes income at 30% and capital gains at an effective 12% inside the policy. For a high-bracket taxpayer that can be worth having, but the exemptions you give up and the five-year rules decide whether it works.
- [Two years on, the savings pot has become an annual habit for many members](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/two-years-on-the-savings-pot-has-become-an-annual-habit): Published 2026-09-30. Administrator data from the first two years of the two-pot system shows that repeat withdrawals, not one-off emergencies, are now the dominant pattern. The arithmetic of that habit deserves a closer look.
- [When a platform moves money offshore, the allowance it uses is still yours](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/when-a-platform-uses-your-offshore-allowance): Published 2026-09-30. A High Court judgment has put a spotlight on how third-party platforms externalise client funds. If your annual offshore allowances were used, the exchange control record carries your name, not the platform's.
- [Women are 58% of credit-active South Africans, and hold 46% of the balances](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/women-hold-58-percent-of-south-africas-credit-agreements): Published 2026-09-30. New credit bureau analysis shows women borrowing more often than men but in smaller, unsecured amounts. The gap between how often you borrow and what you borrow for is a planning problem worth naming.
- [The official interest rate is 8.25% from 1 October, and your trust loan follows it](https://www.navigatewealth.co/resources/article/the-official-interest-rate-is-8-25-from-1-october-and-your-trust-loan-follows-it): Published 2026-09-30.
